newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Netanyahu drops "Lebanon-first" peace bid.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Netanyahu drops "Lebanon-first" peace bid.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said in an interview published on Wednesday he had dropped his proposal to negotiate a deal with Syria on Lebanon first.
Syria, the main power broker in Lebanon, long ago spurned Netanyahu's offer to withdraw Israeli troops from a south Lebanon occupation zone in return for the right security measures from Syria.
Damascus rejected the so-called "Lebanon-first" proposal as a ploy to avoid returning the Golan Heights captured from Syria in the 1967 Middle East War.
"I would have been happy to divide the package, but I don't believe it's practical," Netanyahu told the newspaper Haaretz in the interview.

"It's crystal clear the government of Lebanon, which is able to deploy in the south and create the barrier needed against Hizbollah, won't do that without a green light from Syria, and it's doubtful Syria would give such a green light without an overall agreement," he said.
Syria demands Israel return the strategic heights. Netanyahu insists on keeping them. Israel's on-again, off-again peace talks with Syria, launched in 1991, have been frozen since last year.

Israeli troops and their Lebanese militia allies patrol a south Lebanon occupation zone set up to keep guerrillas from attacking the northern Israeli border. Syria has some 35,000 soldiers in Lebanon.
